subject: MedForge Community Makerspace
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed MedForge Community Makerspace Executive Director Trey Winter regarding the organization's background, current programming, facility search, and upcoming Halloween fundraiser.

items.title: Guest Introduction and Personal Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Trey Winter, Executive Director of MedForge Community Makerspace, who shared his background and move to Medford.

items.title: Founding and Vision of MedForge
items.summary: Winter explained how taking a welding class inspired him to launch MedForge to meet local demand for shared tool access and collaborative space.

items.title: Facility Search and MassDevelopment Grant
items.summary: Winter detailed efforts to secure a 10,000-square-foot facility and highlighted a $1.3 million MassDevelopment grant application submitted with Ware Street Workplaces for 400 Riverside Avenue.

items.title: Community Impact and Economic Value
items.summary: Winter discussed how makerspaces support trade skill development, intergenerational knowledge sharing, and local economic retention.

items.title: Local Partnerships and Household Tool Classes
items.summary: Winter highlighted collaborations with Arts Collaborative Medford and the Medford Public Library, alongside a grant-funded home repair workshop series.

items.title: Welcome to Deadford Halloween Fundraiser
items.summary: Winter announced the October 31 "Welcome to Deadford" Halloween fundraiser at Arts Collaborative Medford, featuring maker-crafted decor, local vendors, and a safe-ride discount.

items.title: Future Events and Membership Structure
items.summary: Winter outlined upcoming workshops, plans for Open Studios demonstrations, and a flexible membership model that includes volunteer options.
